items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Teddy Reig had a notion that I could write for singers with the Basie band... on the strength of that I began to do other things for the Basie band

ctx.x: When you wrote for the Basie band, were there particular soloists at that time that you kept in mind?

Well the things I did for Basie, if I can remember, were as it happened, I think Teddy Reig had a notion that I could write for singers with the Basie band. I think the first thing I did was something or other for a television show, and I don’t remember who the singer was, and on the strength of that I began to do other things for the Basie band in a similar way. I did an album for Arthur Prysock and I remember that Prysock’s key turned out to be E major, an unusual one.
